krum_detection_rate_note: 0.00% in every one of the 25 rounds (25/25) — the head-only attack was never detected, not even once.
krum_score_ratio_note: byz_mean_score / honest_mean_score stayed essentially constant at ~0.38 across all 25 rounds (min 0.37967, max 0.37993). A ratio below 1.0 means the Byzantine clients' plaintext-slice scores were consistently LOWER (more trusted) than the average honest client's score, not merely close enough to hide — they looked more central than a typical honest update, every round.
per_class_f1_note: Normal — normally one of the easiest classes — never once produced a usable F1 score across all 25 rounds. Loss stayed pinned around 2.0 the entire run instead of converging, consistent with the poisoned classifier head being re-corrupted every round faster than honest local training could correct it.

locked_clean_application_baseline_round2.source: master doc, 'NEW Locked Baselines' section, no attack no defence

earlier_flawed_he_krum_hybrid_run.note: This was the run where the attack skipped local training entirely, producing a trivially-detectable frozen-parameter signature. Krum caught it 100% of the time in that run, so F1 tracked close to the clean baseline. Included here ONLY as a contrast case, not a valid Experiment 2 result — see run notes.

headline_finding: With a properly-implemented head-only Byzantine attack (full local training on the backbone, poisoning applied only to classifier.* keys before encryption), adaptive Krum's plaintext-slice scoring achieved 0% detection across all 25 rounds, and the undetected poisoning produced an 82% relative drop in best F1-Macro versus the clean baseline (0.1310 vs 0.7293), with the Normal class permanently at F1=0.0 for the entire run. This is a concrete, measured confirmation of the architectural blind spot predicted for partial (classifier-head-only) HE: encrypting only a slice of the model creates a slice Krum cannot see into, and a client that trains honestly everywhere except that slice is indistinguishable from an honest client by plaintext-distance-based defences.
